<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par127 />genitive), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־יְמִינִי}} (see {{GHGpar|86|h}}) ''a Benjamite'', {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־הַיְמִינִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=15}}, &c., ''the Benjamite''; {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽית־הַלַּחְמִי|translate=the Bethlehemite}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=1}}, &c. (cf., however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=27|verse=12}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=לַבֵּן יְמִינִי}}); {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽית־הַשִּׁמְשִׁי|translate=the Beth-shemite}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִי הָֽעֶזְרִי|translate=the Abiezrite}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=11}}, &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=34}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|e}}
3. In a few instances the nomen regens appears to be used indefinitely notwithstanding a following determinate genitive; it is not so, however, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=7}}, where the reference is to a well-known fountain; 21:28, where in the original context there must have been some reason for ''the seven ewe lambs of the flock''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=30}} ''the spoil found in the city''; but it often is so before a proper name, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=חַג יְהֹוָה|translate=a feast of the Lord}} (unless it is ''the'' spring festival), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=25}}, and frequently {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה|translate=an abomination unto the Lord}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=19}} ''a virgin of Israel''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=12}} ''a man of Benjamin''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=9|hidebook=1}}; similarly before appellatives with the article (or before a genitive determined by a suffix, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=34}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=20}} ''three arrows''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶלְקַת הַשָּׂדֶה|translate=a plot of the ground}} (but see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=32}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=11}}, 13 f., 5:13, 7:3, 8:2. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר הַמַּֽעֲלוֹת}} in the titles of Psalms 120 to 134 (except 121:1, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר לַמַּֽעֲלוֹת}}) was most probably originally the title of a collection, in the sense of ''‘the pilgrimage-songs’'' (according to {{GHGpar|124|r}}), and was subsequently added to these Psalms severally.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָל־הַמָּקוֹם|translate=in all the place}}, sc. of the sanctuary, is a dogmatic correction of {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָל־מָקוֹם}}, ''in every place'', to avoid the difficulty that several holy-places are here authorized, instead of the one central sanctuary. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=13}} also {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הַמָּקוֹם}} (unless it means ''in the whole place'') is remarkable, since elsewhere ''every place'' is always (8 times) {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־מָקוֹם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|f}}
4. The deviations mentioned under ''e'', from a fundamental rule of syntax, are in some cases open to suspicion on textual grounds, but much more doubtful are the instances in which the article is found before a noun already determined in some other way, as—

(''a'') Before a noun which appears to be determined by a following independent determinate genitive. The least questionable are the instances in which the genitive is a ''proper name'', since these may be elliptical forms of expression like the apparent construction of proper names with a genitive, noticed in {{GHGpar|125|h}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנְּחָלִים אַרְנוֹן|translate=the valleys}}, namely the valleys ''of Arnon''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבַּח בֵּית־אֵל|translate=the altar}}, namely the altar of ''Bethel'' (i.e. with the suppression of the real nomen regens, {{GHGheb|text=מִזְבַּח}} without the article; by the pointing {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבַּח}} the Masora evidently intends to allow the choice either of reading {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבֵּחַ}} or correcting it to {{GHGheb|text=מִזְבַּח}}); {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל בֵּית־אֵל|translate=the God of Beth-el}}<ref>According to Philippi ({{GHGterm|st. constr.}}, p. 38) {{GHGheb|text=בית־אל}} is rather a case of ‘sub-position’ in the accusative, as also {{GHGheb|text=הַדֶּ֫רֶךְ חֶתְלוֹן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=15}} (for which, however, in 48:1 there is the correct reading {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫רֶךְ חֶתְלוֹן}}) ''by the way to Hethlon''; and in fact, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=15}} may without difficulty be explained in this way; so {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=39|verse=27}} as an accusative of the material.</ref> (equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל אֵל בּ׳}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=13}} (the LXX read {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם|translate=the God who appeared to thee in the}} holy ''place''); {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר|translate=the king of Assyria}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=16}} (probably a scribal error due to verse 13; it does not occur in the parallel passage, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=31}}), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=13|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=15}}; in the vocative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=13}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=שָׂרָה אִמּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=67}} is no doubt<section end=par127 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
